topic: Offline Coding Agents: Single-Binary AI Development Tools

key_points: Ante (Antigma Labs) is packaged as a single binary that runs offline
One artifact to drop on a machine, no cloud control plane, no install tree
Runs opposite the prevailing shape of the category: thin clients for hosted frontier models
Hit HN (102 points, 65 comments in ~5 hours) as an early Show HN, not a product launch
Positioned in the growing lane of local-first agent runners
OpenCode: 172K GitHub stars, MIT, 75+ LLM providers via Models.dev, TUI Mission Control, works with Ollama
Philosophy = provider agnostic / maximum flexibility; MCP + LSP support
Aider: Git-native precision, Apache 2.0 (46K stars), commit hooks via codebase mapping, any OpenAI-compatible model incl. Ollama
Goose: planning-first orchestration, Apache 2.0 (38K stars), multi-model config
Pi: ultra-minimal harness, MIT (62K stars), 20+ providers
Genuine offline requires 3 things: model runs locally, IDE works with zero internet (no license check/telemetry), no background egress
Standalone desktop apps shipping everything in one binary have the best offline story
Most 'local AI' tools still phone home via telemetry or CDN asset fetch
Hardware defines the ceiling: 6-8GB VRAM = autocomplete, 8-12GB = multi-file edits, 12-16GB = Devstral Small 2 24B (68% SWE-bench Verified), 16-24GB = Qwen3.6-27B (77.2% SWE-bench Verified)
Stand-alone agents detach from the editor; pair with your own IDE choice
Goose: vendor-neutral OSS, 70+ MCP extensions, Linux Foundation (AAIF) stewardship, any LLM provider
Cline: VS Code extension, Apache 2.0 BYOK, MCP-native with tool-creation on demand
Aider: no native MCP; Claude Code: first-party, MCP-native, included in Pro/Max
Autocomplete vs agent vs IDE-native are three different product categories

Enterprise air-gap/offline tools: AirgapAI Code ($1,999 one-time, perpetual license, no license callback), Tabnine, Tabby (Apache 2.0 free), Continue.dev (free), Cline (free), Cody ($59/u/mo), GitHub Copilot
Defense, government, finance, healthcare, CUI/ITAR/classified data can't send code to cloud
Open-source harnesses (Continue, Tabby, Cline) sit alongside commercial on-prem tiers
Compliance posture (SOC 2, FedRAMP, IL5, ITAR/EAR) matters for procurement

stats.fact: Ante hit 102 points and 65 comments on Hacker News within ~5 hours of its Show HN for being a single-binary offline coding agent
OpenCode is the most popular open-source AI coding agent at ~172K GitHub stars (MIT license), ahead of Aider (~46K), Goose (~38K), and Pi (~62K)
Qwen3.6-27B Q4 (16-24GB VRAM) is the gold-standard local coding model at 77.2% SWE-bench Verified; Devstral Small 2 24B Q4 (12-16GB) reaches 68%
4GB VRAM is the absolute floor for local coding inference, delivering only 3-8 tokens/sec with small models; CPU inference is 'too slow for interactive coding'
DDN's 2026 State of AI Infrastructure report found 98% of organizations face AI infrastructure skills gaps
DeepSeek Coder 33B claims ~95% code correctness as the best free local coding model, needing 32GB+ RAM or 24GB VRAM; runs fully offline via Ollama
Air-gapped commercial coding assistants start around $1,999 one-time (AirgapAI Code) vs free Apache-2.0 open-source harnesses like Tabby, Continue.dev, and Cline

angles: Distribution is the new battleground: single-binary offline delivery stands opposite the prevailing 'thin client for a hosted frontier model' shape — no cloud control plane, no install tree, one artifact dropped on a machine

'Offline' is a spectrum, not a binary: many tools claim local models but still phone home via telemetry, license checks, update pings, or CDN asset fetches — genuine offline fails all three runtime checks
The hardware ceiling is the real bottleneck: VRAM tier maps directly to SWE-bench quality, so tool choice is inseparable from the machine you run it on

Open-source freedom vs commercial convenience: MIT/Apache OSS agents (OpenCode, Aider, Goose, Cline) give provider portability and air-gap freedom, while enterprise products sell compliance (SOC 2, FedRAMP, IL5, ITAR) and support
MCP is becoming the offline agent differentiator: Goose ships 70+ MCP extensions out of the box, Cline is MCP-native, OpenCode supports MCP+LSP — while Aider ships without native MCP
Regulated industries (defense, government, finance, healthcare, CUI/ITAR data) are the strongest driver pushing coding agents fully offline
You're not locked into an editor: stand-alone CLI agents detach from the IDE, so you keep your editor and swap the agent — the antithesis of IDE-native bundles like Cursor Composer
